Sample review, 2026-10-22

Verdicts

CrYpToR v2.2 / Universal Polymorphic Device v2.2 demo (dac346b53062):
MALICIOUS. The banner is consistent with an active nonresident COM virus,
not merely an encryption demonstration. A training/collection deployment
could explain possession, but no such deployment context was supplied.
Actual host modification and propagation outweigh the demo disclaimer.

bef140a1a969: BENIGN. All 92 bytes are an HTML 504 Gateway Time-out heading
and a server timeout message. There are no scripts, links, forms, redirects,
encoded payloads, external URLs, dependencies or archive members. The source
may have collected a failed response from a malware URL or inherited a URL's
reputation. Its original collection URL and intended payload are unavailable;
that explanation is plausible, not verified. No trait correction was needed.

AutoRun configuration (2c8d26173558): MALICIOUS. These 69 bytes declare a
relative csrsc.exe launch and icon while advertising the action as Documents.
The CSRSS-like basename at the media root and content-browsing label together
favor deceptive execution over an ordinary branded installer. Autorun itself
is legitimate functionality. The payload is absent, so this file does not
prove replication, C2, exfiltration or a particular worm family. Its original
placement as autorun.inf, Windows version/policy and whether the payload was
present are unknown. The two deception findings remain suspicious; no extra
hostile finding was invented to claim unseen payload behavior.

Reference for the AutoRun interpretation:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/autorun-cmds
Action is AutoPlay display text, not a command. ShellExecute names the target;
an executable target is launched when the applicable AutoRun/AutoPlay action
is honored. Behavior depends on Windows policy, version and media context.

DOS reverse engineering

Rizin x86/16-bit disassembly uses a COM origin of 0100h. At 010Bh the program
masks PIC bits 1Ah, queues keyboard words and reaches 0258h. CALL 072Dh pushes
025Ch; the handler pops that value and subtracts 025Ch to obtain its base.
It saves the DOS DTA (AH=2Fh), selects its own DTA (AH=1Ah), and uses AH=4Eh
and AH=4Fh to enumerate *.COM. At 0772h, AX=3D02h opens the selected DTA
filename read/write. AH=3Fh reads four entry bytes. A fourth-byte 24h marker
skips existing infections. AX=4202h obtains EOF, rejects large/high-word sizes
and files below 1000 bytes, then EOF-3 is saved at header+1 (BP+0855h).

The code at 07AEh supplies its own body to the engine at 14E1h twice. Engine
flags differ between calls. BIOS INT 1Ah and PIT port 40h seed a rotate/XOR
state mixer at 093Dh. Opcode construction chooses instruction/register forms
and writes paired instruction words through the emitter at 099Ch. The output
pointer is saved at 15FFh, adjusted at 165Dh, and invoked through that exact
pointer cell at 16B9h, transforming the copied body. This is generated code
and encryption machinery, not evidence inferred from entropy or a name.

At 07D5h the generated buffer is written at EOF. AX=4200h rewinds the same
handle. AH=40h/CX=4 writes an E9 jump and marker from BP+0854h. It closes the
file and continues enumeration, restores the DTA, clears its working memory
and transfers control back to 0100h. This sample has no network references.

A Unicorn 16-bit harness intercepted every interrupt and port operation and
used only an in-memory 2000-byte host. The original sample, without byte
changes, read four entry bytes, sought to 2000, appended 6608 generated bytes,
sought to zero and wrote E9 CD 07 24. A different timer seed produced 6534
appended bytes with different content. Both runs executed the generated
transform and terminated normally. No native DOS code or host filesystem
infection was executed. Harness, disassembly, infected in-memory outputs and
execution event logs are retained in the task scratch/review directory;
those generated hosts are experimental outputs, not recovered originals.

Rule changes and preservation audit

1. Extended the existing COM append/entry-jump matcher for DI-sourced generated
   bodies and four-byte jump-plus-marker headers. It still binds EOF-3's
   destination to the subsequently written E9 header. The old branch is
   retained. Added a neutral paired-code-buffer generator observation and a
   timer-seeded PRNG observation. Their conjunction with the infector supports
   the separate hostile polymorphic-concealment finding.
2. Moved CALL/POP BX and AL=2/near-CALL byte observations from infection/evasion
   to metadata/binary/code/control-transfer, preserving matcher, confidence,
   criticality, effective file types, platforms and size bounds. Neither
   alone proves an infection or concealment. Exact references were updated.
   Broad anti-static consumers are source-language scoped and do not consume
   these DOS observations; broader metadata consumers were also inspected.
3. Moved AutoRun display and executable-target directives out of the config
   pathname directory to os/autorun/media, preserving effective scopes and
   matching. Corrected Action's unsupported 'command' description to display
   text. Exact and ancestor-selector consumers were inspected. For the broad
   fs/ profile consumers, a disjoint alternative preserves the old one-role
   contribution: moved AutoRun fields count only when no remaining fs/ trait
   matches. This avoids double-counting after relocation.
4. Added suspicious Documents-label execution and CSRSS-like root-target
   observations. A changed payload basename still triggers the document lure;
   another last-letter CSRSS substitution still triggers the naming signal.
   These signatures do not depend on the collector's filename or csrsc.exe.
   New deception rules conservatively require one INI section. Tightened the
   existing neutral launch composite to bind its launch to an AutoRun section.
   Previously, [autorun] followed by [other]/shellexecute=... falsely asserted
   an AutoRun launch. That unsupported match is the intentional loss.
5. Existing launch-composite consumers (Recycler, Recycled, PIF and svchost
   masquerade) and the existing autorun-inf-launch fixtures were inspected.
   Focused Recycler and PIF controls retain their attack detections; an ordinary
   multi-section installer retains its correct neutral launch observation.

The generic INI-header guard is baseline format structure. Full validation
matched it on testdata/benign/php-ini-empty-prepend-append-controls.ini: an
ordinary [PHP] section with empty prepend/append values, not a new capability
or identity. Its initial notable severity overstated that routine property.
The matcher is retained, and its only direct consumers are the two new
AutoRun rules' section-scope exclusions; those exclusions still operate at
baseline. This correction changes no original sample finding or verdict.

Verification and classifier comparison

atomscan --no-update --mode slow --format json and cleave facts were run on
all three original paths. All have zero archive members. Cleave facts supplied
raw/decoded text, symbols, references and metrics; no hidden dependencies or
encoded payloads were present in the two text artifacts. A HEAD-based trait
snapshot was used for the before comparison, without changing the worktree.

All 39 existing testdata/hostile/dos-com fixtures retain every finding after
mapping the two relocated IDs. In particular week-1614 retains its CALL/POP BX
observation and boot-cruel-1022 retains its infection, disk-hook and CMOS attack
coverage. No new unrelated attacks fired in that corpus. Original-sample
findings are preserved under the relocated IDs. Fifteen focused cases pass,
including real-original hashes, operand/entry-byte near misses, renamed-target
positives, actual data-file launches, installers, icon-only names, absolute
System32 paths, cross-section negatives, and Recycler/PIF attack controls.
Run: CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 python3 testdata/triage/cryptor-autorun/check.py

DOS: 14 -> 20 findings, zero -> two hostile and one suspicious. Selected ML
probability 0.23462145 (benign) -> 0.936498 (hostile; dos_com route cls=2).
HTML: one accurate metadata finding unchanged; ML probability 0.00001896421,
benign before and after.
AutoRun: five -> 10 findings, zero -> two suspicious; ML probability
0.000057478745 -> 0.96312195. The classifier still emits cls=0, lvl=-1
(benign). This is a remaining calibrated classifier miss despite supported
deception traits; accurate rules were not inflated or duplicated to force it.
The scanner also reports an installed v18 model versus v19 extractor feature
schema. That is a model/tooling limitation, not a YAML behavior correction.
